sentences.cn: 音乐可以通过……改变某个场所或活动的氛围。
sentences.example: Music can change the atmosphere of a film scene by creating tension before anything happens.

writingIdeas.viewpoint: Music education benefits children beyond performance skills.
writingIdeas.topicSentence: Learning music can develop attention, cooperation and disciplined practice.
writingIdeas.argument: Playing an instrument requires a learner to notice timing, pitch and small errors. Progress is gradual, so children experience the connection between repeated practice and improvement. Group performance adds another demand because each musician must listen and adjust to others. These habits can transfer to collaborative schoolwork, even if the child never becomes a professional performer. Music education is therefore valuable as a process, not only for producing concerts.

writingIdeas.viewpoint: Streaming has widened access but weakened income for some musicians.
writingIdeas.topicSentence: Easy digital access has changed how recorded music is valued and financed.
writingIdeas.argument: Listeners can explore an enormous range of music at relatively low cost, and unknown artists can distribute work internationally. Payment per stream, however, is often too small to support musicians without very large audiences. Independent performers may therefore depend on concerts, teaching or merchandise. Platforms should provide clearer payment information, while listeners can support artists through direct purchases. Wider access is positive, but a sustainable system must also reward creation.

speaking.question: When do you usually listen to music?
speaking.answer: Mostly when I’m travelling or doing something repetitive at home. Music makes a crowded journey feel shorter, and it adds energy when I’m cleaning. I don’t usually play it while reading because lyrics compete with the words on the page. If I need background sound for work, I choose something instrumental and fairly quiet.

speaking.question: Have your musical tastes changed over time?
speaking.answer: Quite a lot. As a teenager I mainly listened to whatever my friends liked, which was mostly pop music. Later I discovered jazz through a film soundtrack and started paying more attention to instruments rather than just lyrics. I still enjoy some old pop songs, but now my playlists are much less predictable and include music from several countries.

reading.title: Before Music Could Be Recorded
paragraphs: Before sound recording, every musical performance was temporary. A melody could survive through memory, written notation or repeated performance, but each version differed slightly. Music was therefore closely tied to a place and occasion: a song belonged to a ceremony, a workplace, a family or a group of travelling performers. Hearing the same performance twice was impossible.

The arrival of commercial recording changed both listening and composition. Performers could be heard by people they would never meet, while listeners could compare interpretations repeatedly. Early recordings were limited in length, so musicians sometimes shortened pieces or reorganised them to fit the available format. Technology did not simply preserve music; it influenced what was produced.

Recording also created the idea of a definitive version. Small variations that would be natural in a live tradition began to sound like mistakes when compared with a familiar record. Studio techniques later allowed artists to combine separate attempts, correct individual notes and add effects that could not be reproduced easily on stage. The finished track became an object in its own right rather than a transparent copy of a performance.

Digital tools have extended this separation. A musician can now record parts in different countries, and software can imitate instruments or alter a voice. At the same time, live concerts remain attractive precisely because they cannot be repeated perfectly. The audience shares an uncertain event in real time. Recorded and live music now serve different expectations: one offers control and unlimited replay, while the other restores the possibility that something unique will happen.

Recording has also changed musical memory. Listeners no longer need to reproduce a song in order to keep it; they can return to exactly the same track. This accuracy preserves detail, but communal variation may decline when one commercial version becomes dominant. The technology that protects a performance can therefore narrow the range of versions people expect to hear.
